mutant.description: Readers were shown able to go both ways rather than assumed. (1) The issuer recorded both criteria FAILing pre-cut (AC1 because the live CodeSha256 was the rollback hash and the live zip had no trading_calendar.py; AC2 because the record was absent); after the work AC1 reads PASS, so it is not stuck-FAIL. (2) AC2 still reads FAIL, and the cause was isolated to its own retrieval by reproducing its exact query and then running the same window with the filter removed -- the second read found the line the first could not, which separates 'the world is wrong' from 'the instrument cannot see'. (3) The gate chain discriminates: on the sibling order the naming plan gate REFUSED an addition and later read CONFORMANT once the name changed, and here safe-apply's limbs passed while that same gate only WARNed on existing resources.
mutant.expected: AC1 moves FAIL -> PASS across the apply; AC2's failure is attributable to its filter, demonstrated by the same query minus the filter returning the required line; and no control passes merely because nothing was looked at.
mutant.observed: AC1 PASS against its recorded pre-cut FAIL. AC2 FAIL, with its own query returning 3 events (START, END, REPORT) and the unfiltered control returning 7 including the SKIP line, 'is not the production T-1' present True and 'dispatched: doc=' present False. The Arm 1 controls held: ssm list-commands for advi-49f-chain-dispatch read 181 before and 181 after with zero new CommandIds, and the host read running before and after. FOLLOW-UP, after the issuer repaired the instrument at f5caf28329: AC2 moved FAIL -> PASS with the DEPLOY UNCHANGED -- same RequestId, same single invoke, same record -- which is the cleanest possible demonstration that the original FAIL was the retrieval and not the world, and that this criterion is not stuck in either direction.
